_meta.notes: Country-scoped curated nodes; link via relationships during ingest.

910.name: Volcanic Formation and Uninhabited Islands
910.label: Event
910.description: São Tomé and Príncipe form as volcanic islands on the Cameroon Line; unlike most African territories, the islands were uninhabited before Portuguese arrival.

910.name: Geological Origins and Cameroon Line
910.label: Event
910.description: Volcanic islands formed along the Cameroon Line hotspot chain; Pico de São Tomé (2,024m) and Pico do Príncipe; unique biodiversity evolves in isolation.

910.name: Pre-Discovery Ecology and Endemism
910.label: Event
910.description: Islands develop extraordinary endemic species: giant sunbird, São Tomé ibis, and unique plant species; no human settlement before 1470.

920.name: Portuguese Discovery and First Settlement
920.label: Event
920.description: Portuguese navigators discover the islands c.1470–1471; initial colonisation with degredados (exiled convicts), Jewish children, and enslaved Africans.

920.name: Discovery and Initial Colonisation
920.label: Event
920.description: João de Santarém and Pêro Escobar reach São Tomé (c.1470) and Príncipe (1471); first settlers include Portuguese degredados and Jewish children exiled from Portugal.

920.name: Early Sugar Plantation Economy
920.label: Event
920.description: Álvaro de Caminha establishes sugar plantations using enslaved African labour; São Tomé becomes the world's largest sugar producer by the 1520s; model later exported to Brazil.

930.name: Sugar Economy and Atlantic Slave Trade Hub
930.label: Event
930.description: São Tomé serves as a critical entrepôt in the Atlantic slave trade; sugar production declines as Brazilian competition rises; mixed-race forro community emerges.

930.name: Slave Trade Entrepôt
930.label: Event
930.description: São Tomé becomes a major staging post for the Atlantic slave trade between West Africa and the Americas; tens of thousands pass through annually.

930.name: Slave Revolts and Angolares
930.label: Event
930.description: Major slave revolt led by Amador 1595; escaped slaves (angolares) establish independent maroon communities in the island interior; Amador briefly captures the capital.

940.name: Cocoa Economy and Roça Plantation System
940.label: Event
940.description: Cocoa replaces sugar; São Tomé becomes the world's largest cocoa producer by 1908; the roça plantation system uses contract labourers (serviçais) in conditions of virtual slavery.

940.name: Cocoa Revolution and 'Islands of Chocolate'
940.label: Event
940.description: Cocoa introduced early 19th century; massive expansion under Portuguese planters; São Tomé becomes world's largest cocoa producer by 1908; known as 'the chocolate islands'.

940.name: Roça System and Cadbury Boycott
940.label: Event
940.description: Roça (plantation) system uses contract labourers (serviçais) from Angola, Mozambique, and Cape Verde in conditions of virtual slavery; Cadbury chocolate boycott 1909 draws international attention.

950.name: Independence Movement and MLSTP
950.label: Event
950.description: The MLSTP (Movimento de Libertação de São Tomé e Príncipe) leads the independence struggle from exile; Carnation Revolution in Portugal enables independence.

950.name: MLSTP Formation and Exile Struggle
950.label: Event
950.description: Manuel Pinto da Costa and others found the MLSTP in exile (Libreville, then Accra); linked to other Portuguese African liberation movements; limited guerrilla capacity.

950.name: Independence (12 July 1975)
950.label: Event
950.description: Portuguese Carnation Revolution April 1974 ends dictatorship; negotiations lead to independence 12 July 1975; Manuel Pinto da Costa becomes first president; MLSTP single-party socialist state.

950.name: Socialist Single-Party Period
950.label: Event
950.description: MLSTP single-party socialist state; nationalisation of roças; economic decline; dependence on Soviet bloc and Angola; forced democratic opening.

950.name: Nationalisation and Economic Decline
950.label: Event
950.description: Plantations nationalised; Portuguese managers flee; cocoa production collapses; food shortages; dependence on foreign aid.

950.name: Mercenary Invasion Attempt (1978)
950.label: Event
950.description: Alleged mercenary plot to overthrow government; Angolan troops stationed as deterrent; heightened security and political repression.

960.name: Democratic Transition
960.label: Event
960.description: São Tomé becomes one of Africa's first multiparty democracies; Miguel Trovoada elected 1991; political instability but democratic norms generally hold.

960.name: Multiparty Democracy Established
960.label: Event
960.description: 1990 referendum approves multiparty constitution; Miguel Trovoada wins 1991 election; first peaceful transfer of power in lusophone Africa; Fradique de Menezes elected 2001.

960.name: 2003 Mini-Coup
960.label: Event
960.description: Military officers briefly seize power while President Menezes is abroad; international mediation by Nigeria; democratic rule restored within a week.

960.name: Contemporary São Tomé and Príncipe
960.label: Event
960.description: Oil exploration raises hopes and corruption risks; democratic consolidation; tourism potential; climate vulnerability of small island state.

960.name: Oil Exploration and Economic Hopes
960.label: Event
960.description: Joint Development Zone with Nigeria; oil exploration raises expectations of wealth; corruption concerns; actual production remains minimal.

960.name: Democratic Consolidation and Fragile Economy
960.label: Event
960.description: Regular democratic elections; coalition politics; heavy aid dependence; cocoa still dominant export; ecotourism development; vulnerability to climate change and sea-level rise.
